doc.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024

title: Sun Ra, George Clinton and showmanship
summary: Sun Ra as attention seeker and influence on Clinton; seeing and hearing together makes a monster entertainer.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I didn’t know too much about Sun Ra. But my drummer played with him and we talk about him often you know. And he was an attention mongrel. He wanted attention so he created this, from the sky, much like George Clinton. You know I think George kind of learned a lot from him.

It’s funny you say that because the reason I brought it up, I was looking at some “Parliament Funkadelic” video this morning and it made me think of Sun Ra. Like these guys had the same kind of outrageous, look-at-me type approach.

Yeah. And I think more people look at people than listen to them you know? But if you put them both together, like Bootsie. Bootsie is a person that has the funk in his body but he looked like a star child. Like he had — you see him before you hear him but then you
might hear him before you see him. But if you put the two together you’ve got a monster entertainer. You know? So that’s the way George Clinton is too you know.
